question: ________ describe the idea of evolution in his book, “The origin of species”.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Darwin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Darwin **is the correct option as he is the one who proposed the idea of evolution in his book **"The Origin of Species"**.
 
• The main keyword in the question is "evolution", which refers to the process of gradual development and change in species over time.
 
• Edward Jenner is known for developing the smallpox vaccine, which is a significant contribution to medicine.
 
• Robert Brown was a Scottish botanist who discovered the cell nucleus and contributed to the study of plant anatomy.
 
• Aristotle was a Greek philosopher and scientist who made significant contributions to various fields such as biology, physics, and ethics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• English naturalist, geologist, and biologist Charles Robert Darwin is well-known for his contributions to evolutionary biology.
 
• His theory which holds that all living things share a common ancestor—is now widely acknowledged as a cornerstone of science.
 
• He presented his scientific hypothesis which he named natural selection—in a joint publication with Alfred Russel Wallace.
 
• According to this idea, the competition for survival in natural selection has an impact like to that of artificial selection in selective breeding, which leads to the branching pattern of evolution.
